beliefs: f is stochastic: identical inputs give different outputs (1.0 → many values; 3.0 → 10 values; 5.0 → 20 values; -100 → 10 identical values, see next) [E3, E4, E7, E8].
For some inputs the output is constant across repeats (x=-100 → 0.0059 ten times; x=-128 → 0.0046; x=-127.9999 → 0.0046), suggesting a deterministic/quantized region or caching [E1, E5, E8].
For most inputs outputs look like i.i.d. draws from a roughly symmetric distribution centered near 0 with std ~0.1, range about [-0.25, 0.35] [E1-E8].
No smoothness or periodicity: nearby inputs give unrelated values [E2, E3, E6].
Output spread is similar across the domain (large negative, near-zero, large positive) [E5, E8].
Whether an input is 'constant' vs 'noisy' is not yet predictable from x alone (e.g. -100 constant but -0.25 noisy; 3.0 noisy) — possibly a hidden interval or rule [E8]?
notes: Added the striking new fact from E8 that some inputs (like -100) return a fixed value on every repeat while others are noisy; kept the i.i.d. Gaussian model for the noisy case since it still fits the bulk of the data, and flagged the constant-vs-noisy rule as unknown.
